subject: Persistence of Memory
hook: PERSISTENCE OF MEMORY IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The melting clocks in Salvador Dalí's 'The Persistence of Memory' were not inspired by Albert Einstein's theory of relativity, but by the artist's observation of Camembert cheese melting in the sun.
angle_support: Asked by Ilya Prigogine whether this was the case, Dalí replied that the soft watches were not inspired by the theory of relativity, but by the surrealist perception of a Camembert melting in the sun.
As Dawn Adès wrote, 'The soft watches are an unconscious symbol of the relativity of space and time, a Surrealist meditation on the collapse of our notions of a fixed cosmic order'.
title: The True Origin of Dalí's Melting Clocks
description: Discover the surprising, non-scientific inspiration behind Salvador Dalí's most famous painting. It turns out the melting watches were inspired by cheese, not physics.
narration: PERSISTENCE OF MEMORY IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture Einstein’s complex relativity theory behind those famous melting clocks. You assume the physics of space and time dictated the design. It was actually much simpler. When asked if his soft watches were inspired by the theory of relativity, the artist clarified his true muse. He was simply observing a wheel of Camembert cheese melting in the hot sun. That mundane, dairy-based afternoon sparked the iconic surrealist vision. Sometimes a masterpiece is just lunch left out too long.
